title: English High-Frequency Word Symbol Lookup Table

source_basis.name: Oxford English Corpus top common words summary
source_basis.note: Used as a public reference for very high-frequency written English word ordering.

source_basis.name: Google Trillion Word Corpus derived 10,000 word list
source_basis.note: Used as a public reference for broad frequency-priority ordering.

source_basis.name: COCA frequency list references
source_basis.note: Used as a corpus-frequency sanity check; exact ranks differ by corpus and lemmatization.

purpose: Create a symbol lookup table for the most frequent English words, giving higher-frequency words higher priority for compact symbolic conversion.

core_definition.summary: Common English words, especially function words, receive short stable symbols so repeated language can be compressed into symbolic UKR expressions.
core_definition.governing_rule: Frequency determines symbol priority; symbol meaning remains locked to the table and does not override ordinary language context.

core_separation.corrected_equation: symbol = frequency-prioritized shorthand + lookup-table anchor + compression utility
core_separation.one_line_translation: The symbol replaces repeated text for compression; it does not replace meaning, evidence, or context.

symbol_priority_method.rank_source_model: corpus-frequency priority seeded from public English frequency lists
assignment_rules: Rank 1-32: highest-priority core grammar words receive single glyphs first.
Rank 33-85: high-frequency words continue receiving single glyphs.
Rank 86-128: common words receive composite glyphs beginning with ˙.
Rank 129+: extended common words receive composite glyphs beginning with ¨.
The lookup table is authoritative for symbol meaning inside this UKR.
symbol_priority_method.collision_rule: Every word receives one unique symbol string; no two entries share the same symbol.
symbol_priority_method.context_rule: If a word has multiple senses, the symbol compresses the surface word unless a later UKR adds sense-specific disambiguation.

boundary_theorems.meaning: A symbol is not automatic truth.
The lookup table controls symbol meaning.
More common words should be symbolized earlier.

distortion_tests.name: Lookup Anchor Test
distortion_tests.question: Does the symbol map to a defined word in this table?

distortion_tests.name: Collision Test
distortion_tests.question: Does another word already use this symbol?

distortion_tests.name: Context Drift Test
distortion_tests.question: Is someone assigning extra meaning not present in the lookup table?

distortion_tests.name: Frequency Priority Test
distortion_tests.question: Are the highest-frequency words receiving the shortest symbols?

failure_modes.name: Symbol Drift
failure_modes.description: The symbol is used for meanings outside its assigned word.

failure_modes.name: Collision Confusion
failure_modes.description: Two words are accidentally assigned the same symbol.

failure_modes.name: Mystical Inflation
failure_modes.description: A compression symbol is treated as occult, spiritual, or evidentiary proof.

failure_modes.name: Context Erasure
failure_modes.description: Polysemous words are compressed without preserving sentence context.

one_line_translation: High-frequency English words get the shortest stable symbols first, creating a lookup table for compact UKR text compression.
